∫ex(1−x1+x2)2dx\displaystyle\int e^x\left(\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x^2}\right)^2 dx∫ex(1+x21−x​)2dx is equal to:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea ∫ex [f(x)+f′(x)] dx=exf(x)+C\displaystyle\int e^x\,[f(x) + f'(x)]\,dx = e^x f(x) + C∫ex[f(x)+f′(x)]dx=exf(x)+C

  1. 1

    Expand (1−x)2=(1+x2)−2x(1 - x)^2 = (1 + x^2) - 2x(1−x)2=(1+x2)−2x

    (1−x1+x2)2=11+x2−2x(1+x2)2\left(\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x^2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2} - \dfrac{2x}{\left(1 + x^2\right)^2}(1+x21−x​)2=1+x21​−(1+x2)22x​(1−x1+x2)2=11+x2−2x(1+x2)2\displaystyle \left(\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x^2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2} - \dfrac{2x}{\left(1 + x^2\right)^2}(1+x21−x​)2=1+x21​−(1+x2)22x​
  2. 2

    Take f(x)=11+x2f(x) = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}f(x)=1+x21​

    f′(x)=−2x(1+x2)2f'(x) = -\dfrac{2x}{\left(1 + x^2\right)^2}f′(x)=−(1+x2)22x​f′(x)=−2x(1+x2)2\displaystyle f'(x) = -\dfrac{2x}{\left(1 + x^2\right)^2}f′(x)=−(1+x2)22x​
  3. 3

    So the integrand is ex[f(x)+f′(x)]e^x[f(x) + f'(x)]ex[f(x)+f′(x)]

    ∫ex[11+x2−2x(1+x2)2]dx=ex1+x2+C\displaystyle\int e^x\left[\dfrac{1}{1 + x^2} - \dfrac{2x}{(1 + x^2)^2}\right]dx = \dfrac{e^x}{1 + x^2} + C∫ex[1+x21​−(1+x2)22x​]dx=1+x2ex​+C∫ex[11+x2−2x(1+x2)2]dx=ex1+x2+C\displaystyle \displaystyle\int e^x\left[\dfrac{1}{1 + x^2} - \dfrac{2x}{(1 + x^2)^2}\right]dx = \dfrac{e^x}{1 + x^2} + C∫ex[1+x21​−(1+x2)22x​]dx=1+x2ex​+C
    1
Answer(A) ex1+x2+C\displaystyle \dfrac{e^x}{1 + x^2} + C1+x2ex​+C

Watch out Expanding (1−x)2(1 - x)^2(1−x)2 as 1−x21 - x^21−x2; the middle term −2x-2x−2x is what creates f′(x)f'(x)f′(x).

    ∫x31+x2 dx=12∫t−1t dt=12∫(t1/2−t−1/2)dt\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x^3}{\sqrt{1 + x^2}}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{t - 1}{\sqrt t}\,dt = \dfrac{1}{2}\int \left(t^{1/2} - t^{-1/2}\right)dt∫1+x2​x3​dx=21​∫t​t−1​dt=21​∫(t1/2−t−1/2)dt∫x31+x2 dx=12∫t−1t dt=12∫(t1/2−t−1/2)dt\displaystyle \displaystyle\int \dfrac{x^3}{\sqrt{1 + x^2}}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{t - 1}{\sqrt t}\,dt = \dfrac{1}{2}\int \left(t^{1/2} - t^{-1/2}\right)dt∫1+x2​x3​dx=21​∫t​t−1​dt=21​∫(t1/2−t−1/2)dt

The value of ∫01sin⁡−1x dx\displaystyle\int_0^1 \sin^{-1} x\,dx∫01​sin−1xdx is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea By parts with the second function 111: ∫f(x) dx=xf(x)−∫xf′(x) dx\displaystyle\int f(x)\,dx = x f(x) - \int x f'(x)\,dx∫f(x)dx=xf(x)−∫xf′(x)dx

  1. 1

    Integrate by parts, taking sin⁡−1x\sin^{-1} xsin−1x as first function and 111 as second

    ∫sin⁡−1x dx=xsin⁡−1x−∫x1−x2 dx\displaystyle\int \sin^{-1} x\,dx = x\sin^{-1} x - \int \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\,dx∫sin−1xdx=xsin−1x−∫1−x2​x​dx∫sin⁡−1x dx=xsin⁡−1x−∫x1−x2 dx\displaystyle \displaystyle\int \sin^{-1} x\,dx = x\sin^{-1} x - \int \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\,dx∫sin−1xdx=xsin−1x−∫1−x2​x​dx
  2. 2

    Put 1−x2=t1 - x^2 = t1−x2=t in the last integral

    ∫x1−x2 dx=−1−x2\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\,dx = -\sqrt{1 - x^2}∫1−x2​x​dx=−1−x2​∫x1−x2 dx=−1−x2\displaystyle \displaystyle\int \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\,dx = -\sqrt{1 - x^2}∫1−x2​x​dx=−1−x2​
  3. 3

    So

    ∫01sin⁡−1x dx=[xsin⁡−1x+1−x2]01\displaystyle\int_0^1 \sin^{-1} x\,dx = \Big[x\sin^{-1} x + \sqrt{1 - x^2}\Big]_0^1∫01​sin−1xdx=[xsin−1x+1−x2​]01​∫01sin⁡−1x dx=[xsin⁡−1x+1−x2]01\displaystyle \displaystyle\int_0^1 \sin^{-1} x\,dx = \Big[x\sin^{-1} x + \sqrt{1 - x^2}\Big]_0^1∫01​sin−1xdx=[xsin−1x+1−x2​]01​
  4. 4

    Put the limits

    (π2+0)−(0+1)=π2−1\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + 0\right) - (0 + 1) = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 1(2π​+0)−(0+1)=2π​−1(π2+0)−(0+1)=π2−1\displaystyle \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + 0\right) - (0 + 1) = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 1(2π​+0)−(0+1)=2π​−1
    1
Answer(B) π2−1\displaystyle \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 12π​−1

Watch out Choosing (A) by forgetting that 1−x2\sqrt{1 - x^2}1−x2​ equals 111 at the lower limit.

Formula / idea elog⁡m=me^{\log m} = melogm=m; ∫ax dx=axlog⁡a+C\displaystyle\int a^x\,dx = \dfrac{a^x}{\log a} + C∫axdx=logaax​+C

    Use eplog⁡q=elog⁡qp=qpe^{p\log q} = e^{\log q^p} = q^peplogq=elogqp=qp on each term

    exlog⁡a=ax,ealog⁡x=xa,ealog⁡a=aae^{x\log a} = a^x, \qquad e^{a\log x} = x^a, \qquad e^{a\log a} = a^aexloga=ax,ealogx=xa,ealoga=aaexlog⁡a=ax,ealog⁡x=xa,ealog⁡a=aa\displaystyle e^{x\log a} = a^x, \qquad e^{a\log x} = x^a, \qquad e^{a\log a} = a^aexloga=ax,ealogx=xa,ealoga=aa

    ∫(ax+xa+aa)dx=axlog⁡a+xa+1a+1+aax+C\displaystyle\int \left(a^x + x^a + a^a\right)dx = \dfrac{a^x}{\log a} + \dfrac{x^{a + 1}}{a + 1} + a^a x + C∫(ax+xa+aa)dx=logaax​+a+1xa+1​+aax+C∫(ax+xa+aa)dx=axlog⁡a+xa+1a+1+aax+C\displaystyle \displaystyle\int \left(a^x + x^a + a^a\right)dx = \dfrac{a^x}{\log a} + \dfrac{x^{a + 1}}{a + 1} + a^a x + C∫(ax+xa+aa)dx=logaax​+a+1xa+1​+aax+C

Answer(B) axlog⁡a+xa+1a+1+aax+C\displaystyle \dfrac{a^x}{\log a} + \dfrac{x^{a + 1}}{a + 1} + a^a x + Clogaax​+a+1xa+1​+aax+C

Assertion (A): ∫−π/2π/2(x3+xcos⁡x+sin⁡5x+1)dx=π\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \left(x^3 + x\cos x + \sin^5 x + 1\right)dx = \pi∫−π/2π/2​(x3+xcosx+sin5x+1)dx=π. Reason (R): For every function fff continuous on [−a,a][-a, a][−a,a], ∫−aaf(x) dx=2∫0af(x) dx\displaystyle\int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx = 2\int_0^a f(x)\,dx∫−aa​f(x)dx=2∫0a​f(x)dx.

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea On [−a,a][-a, a][−a,a]: an odd function integrates to 000; only an even function gives 2∫0af(x) dx2\displaystyle\int_0^a f(x)\,dx2∫0a​f(x)dx.

  1. 1

    Check A: x3x^3x3, xcos⁡xx\cos xxcosx, sin⁡5x\sin^5 xsin5x are odd, so their integrals are 000

    ∫−π/2π/2(x3+xcos⁡x+sin⁡5x+1)dx=0+∫−π/2π/21 dx=π\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \left(x^3 + x\cos x + \sin^5 x + 1\right)dx = 0 + \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} 1\,dx = \pi∫−π/2π/2​(x3+xcosx+sin5x+1)dx=0+∫−π/2π/2​1dx=π∫−π/2π/2(x3+xcos⁡x+sin⁡5x+1)dx=0+∫−π/2π/21 dx=π\displaystyle \displaystyle\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \left(x^3 + x\cos x + \sin^5 x + 1\right)dx = 0 + \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} 1\,dx = \pi∫−π/2π/2​(x3+xcosx+sin5x+1)dx=0+∫−π/2π/2​1dx=π
  2. 2

    So A is true.

  3. 3

    Check R with f(x)=xf(x) = xf(x)=x on [−1,1][-1, 1][−1,1]

    ∫−11x dx=0,2∫01x dx=1\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} x\,dx = 0, \qquad 2\int_0^1 x\,dx = 1∫−11​xdx=0,2∫01​xdx=1∫−11x dx=0,2∫01x dx=1\displaystyle \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} x\,dx = 0, \qquad 2\int_0^1 x\,dx = 1∫−11​xdx=0,2∫01​xdx=1
  4. 4

    The two sides differ, so R is false (it holds only for even fff).

  5. 5

    A false R cannot explain A.

  6. 6

    Hence the correct option is (C).

    1
Answer(C) A is true, but R is false

Watch out Marking (A) because R looks like a textbook property; it misses the condition that fff must be even.

    I=xcos⁡a+sin⁡a log⁡∣sin⁡(x−a)∣+CI = x\cos a + \sin a\,\log|\sin(x - a)| + CI=xcosa+sinalog∣sin(x−a)∣+CI=xcos⁡a+sin⁡a log⁡∣sin⁡(x−a)∣+C\displaystyle I = x\cos a + \sin a\,\log|\sin(x - a)| + CI=xcosa+sinalog∣sin(x−a)∣+C

    Integrate

    ½

  5. 5

    I2=∫1−1t2(t+1t)2−2 dt=∫dvv2−2=122log⁡∣v−2v+2∣I_2 = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{1 - \frac{1}{t^2}}{\left(t + \frac{1}{t}\right)^2 - 2}\,dt = \int \dfrac{dv}{v^2 - 2} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt 2}\log\left|\dfrac{v - \sqrt 2}{v + \sqrt 2}\right|I2​=∫(t+t1​)2−21−t21​​dt=∫v2−2dv​=22​1​log​v+2​v−2​​​I2=∫1−1t2(t+1t)2−2 dt=∫dvv2−2=122log⁡∣v−2v+2∣\displaystyle I_2 = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{1 - \frac{1}{t^2}}{\left(t + \frac{1}{t}\right)^2 - 2}\,dt = \int \dfrac{dv}{v^2 - 2} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt 2}\log\left|\dfrac{v - \sqrt 2}{v + \sqrt 2}\right|I2​=∫(t+t1​)2−21−t21​​dt=∫v2−2dv​=22​1​log​v+2​v−2​​​

Case Study: In a mathematics quiz, a team is told to use only the property ∫0af(x) dx=∫0af(a−x) dx\displaystyle\int_0^a f(x)\,dx = \int_0^a f(a - x)\,dx∫0a​f(x)dx=∫0a​f(a−x)dx (with standard integrals) to evaluate the integrals below. Answer the following.
  1. (i)Evaluate ∫0π/2log⁡(4+3sin⁡x4+3cos⁡x)dx\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \log\left(\dfrac{4 + 3\sin x}{4 + 3\cos x}\right)dx∫0π/2​log(4+3cosx4+3sinx​)dx.1 mark
  2. (ii)Evaluate ∫02x2−x dx\displaystyle\int_0^2 x\sqrt{2 - x}\,dx∫02​x2−x​dx.1 mark
  3. (iii)Evaluate ∫0π/2sin⁡2xsin⁡x+cos⁡x dx\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\sin^2 x}{\sin x + \cos x}\,dx∫0π/2​sinx+cosxsin2x​dx.2 marks

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Replace xxx by a−xa - xa−x; then add the two forms of III, or integrate the simpler form.

(i)1 mark

  1. 1

    Let

    I=∫0π/2log⁡(4+3sin⁡x4+3cos⁡x)dxI = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \log\left(\dfrac{4 + 3\sin x}{4 + 3\cos x}\right)dxI=∫0π/2​log(4+3cosx4+3sinx​)dxI=∫0π/2log⁡(4+3sin⁡x4+3cos⁡x)dx\displaystyle I = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \log\left(\dfrac{4 + 3\sin x}{4 + 3\cos x}\right)dxI=∫0π/2​log(4+3cosx4+3sinx​)dx
  2. 2

    Replace xxx by π2−x\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x2π​−x; sin⁡\sinsin and cos⁡\coscos swap

    I=∫0π/2log⁡(4+3cos⁡x4+3sin⁡x)dx=−II = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \log\left(\dfrac{4 + 3\cos x}{4 + 3\sin x}\right)dx = -II=∫0π/2​log(4+3sinx4+3cosx​)dx=−II=∫0π/2log⁡(4+3cos⁡x4+3sin⁡x)dx=−I\displaystyle I = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \log\left(\dfrac{4 + 3\cos x}{4 + 3\sin x}\right)dx = -II=∫0π/2​log(4+3sinx4+3cosx​)dx=−I
    ½
  3. 3

    So

    2I=0  ⇒  I=02I = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; I = 02I=0⇒I=0
    ½
Answer (i)0\displaystyle 00

(ii)1 mark

    Let

  2. 2

    Replace xxx by 2−x2 - x2−x; the root becomes x\sqrt xx​

    I=∫02(2−x)x dx=∫02(2x1/2−x3/2)dxI = \displaystyle\int_0^2 (2 - x)\sqrt x\,dx = \int_0^2 \left(2x^{1/2} - x^{3/2}\right)dxI=∫02​(2−x)x​dx=∫02​(2x1/2−x3/2)dxI=∫02(2−x)x dx=∫02(2x1/2−x3/2)dx\displaystyle I = \displaystyle\int_0^2 (2 - x)\sqrt x\,dx = \int_0^2 \left(2x^{1/2} - x^{3/2}\right)dxI=∫02​(2−x)x​dx=∫02​(2x1/2−x3/2)dx

    2I=12[log⁡(2+1)−log⁡(2−1)]=12log⁡(2+1)22I = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}\left[\log\left(\sqrt 2 + 1\right) - \log\left(\sqrt 2 - 1\right)\right] = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}\log\left(\sqrt 2 + 1\right)^22I=2​1​[log(2​+1)−log(2​−1)]=2​1​log(2​+1)22I=12[log⁡(2+1)−log⁡(2−1)]=12log⁡(2+1)2\displaystyle 2I = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}\left[\log\left(\sqrt 2 + 1\right) - \log\left(\sqrt 2 - 1\right)\right] = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}\log\left(\sqrt 2 + 1\right)^22I=2​1​[log(2​+1)−log(2​−1)]=2​1​log(2​+1)2
